issue.title: Project promotion fails 'project anchors could not be persisted' when a concurrent frontmatter write lands after the seed
issue.description:
Reported by Bryan on epic bob-cli-78 (note #1, screenshot 20261013_061115.png): promoting a task to a project
(Ctrl+Shift+Alt+N / createProjectNoteFromTask) shows "Created project, but project anchors could not be
persisted; source task was kept". Four attempts on the MacBook (vault commits 3b478123, bf9ba3f9, 55c4dd0e,
b1302c0c; sase.md ^foo -> sase_foo.md) all failed the same way; nav 2.30.0 was installed there.

Trigger shape: the source task (a) has a live Task Link under today's open Pomodoro ([[sase#^foo]]), so
applyProjectPromotionBacklinkExpansion runs, and (b) has child bullets that the seed converts into new
resident tasks without block IDs, so the promotion must write "project anchors" (new ^ids) into the freshly
seeded project note with a second, preimage-checked write
(670-plugin-project-files.js ~L170 -> 660 writeProjectPromotionFileChange(createdPath, createdFile,
seedContent, updated)). Any change to the new note between the seed write and that anchor write fails the
preimage check. bob-project-tasks reacts to metadataCache "changed" with a 250 ms debounced
processFrontMatter that adds task_count/open_task_count (the failed notes all carry
task_count: 2 / open_task_count: 2), and Templater opens the new note in an editor (create_new_note_from_template(..., true)),
so the editor path compares editor.getValue() too. Promotions without converted children (no anchors to write)
are unaffected, e.g. job_apply_to_databricks on 2026-10-12.

Reproduction (node harness, scripts/test-navigation-hotkeys-forward-promotion.cjs factory): source sase.md
with "- [*] #task foo bar baz [created::2026-10-13] ^foo" + two tab-indented child bullets, today's daily note
"- [ ] (**0600-0610** [t:: 10m]) — BOB / \t- [[sase#^foo]]", cursorLine on ^foo, and a vault.process wrapper that,
right after the seed write to sase_foo.md, inserts "task_count: 2\nopen_task_count: 2" into its frontmatter
(what bob-project-tasks does). Result: "Created project, but project anchors could not be persisted; source
task was kept". Without the frontmatter change it succeeds ("1 link updated"). Identical results on nav 2.13.0
(2e2ce32), 2.29.0 (ace5733) and 2.30.0 (5d6392e), so this predates bob-cli-78; the anchor-write preimage check
dates from 0b6c847 (2026-10-01).

Fix direction: make the anchor write tolerate unrelated concurrent changes to the brand-new note - e.g. fold
the anchors into the seed write (plan targets inside the seed's vault.process callback) so no second write is
needed, or re-read the note and re-plan anchors against current content (body/line-level preimage instead of
whole-file equality, frontmatter changes ignored) and write through vault.process rather than a lagging editor.
Add the reproduction above as a regression test (both closed-editor and open-editor variants), bump
bob-navigation-hotkeys, build/test/validate, and deploy.

task_type_fields.impact: Task-to-project promotion is unusable for linked tasks with child bullets: the project note is created but the source task is kept and links are not expanded, leaving a duplicate to clean up by hand.
task_type_fields.repro: Promote a task that has a live Task Link in today's open Pomodoro and child bullets (converted to new residents) while bob-project-tasks is enabled; harness repro in the description injects task_count frontmatter after the seed write.

issue.creation_reason: Bryan hit this repeatedly while promoting a linked task with child bullets and reported it on bob-cli-78; the land agent reproduced it as a pre-existing race unrelated to the epic.

payload.description: Reported on this epic's note #1 (screenshot); diagnosed during its landing as pre-existing, not caused by the cascade
